population_definition: Biologic-naive Crohn's disease patients initiating ustekinumab (real-world claims cohort)
source: Vu M, Ghosh S, Umashankar K, et al. Comparison of surgery rates in biologic-naive patients with Crohn's disease treated with vedolizumab or ustekinumab: findings from SOJOURN. BMC Gastroenterol. 2023;23:87.
note: CD-related surgery identified from medical claims (CPT/HCPCS/ICD procedure codes): intestinal excision/resection, fistula repair/strictureplasty, abscess drainage. Median follow-up 9.3 months (range 0.4-27.2); cumulative incidence at 1 year reported directly. This is the SAME severity tier (biologic-naive) the response/remission multipliers' UNITI-2/naive side approximates -- used here as this project's naive-population surgery-rate anchor.

population_definition: Crohn's disease patients who failed anti-TNF AND a second-line biologic (vedolizumab or ustekinumab), now starting a THIRD-line biologic
source: Kassouri L, Amiot A, Kirchgesner J, et al. The outcome of Crohn's disease patients refractory to anti-TNF and either vedolizumab or ustekinumab. Dig Liver Dis. 2020;52(10):1148-1155.
note: NOT the same severity tier as this project's refractory scenario (UNITI-1-equivalent: single anti-TNF failure, starting a SECOND-line biologic). This cohort has already failed TWO biologics and is starting a THIRD. No published cohort reporting surgery incidence at the UNITI-1-equivalent (single-failure, second-line) severity tier, matched against a comparably-measured naive rate, was found after an extensive search (see R/utils/refractory_multipliers.R module header). Used as a deliberately conservative/upper-bound proxy, not a matched point estimate -- flagged explicitly wherever this multiplier is used or reported. Surgery definition not specified in the source beyond 'need for surgery' as a Cox regression outcome variable; window is 48 weeks vs. the naive row's 52 weeks (~4-week / ~8% mismatch in follow-up length, treated as negligible relative to the population-severity mismatch, which is the dominant caveat).
